quotations.exact_quotation: Write D \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sum_{t\in T}[t] for the effective divisor on X obtained by taking the formal sum of the points in T, each with multiplicity one; denote the associated line bundle \mathcal{O}_X(D) by \mathcal{L} and the canonical bundle of X by \omega_X.
quotations.source_paragraph: Proof. Since X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) is infinite, we may always adjoin to T extra points of X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) that do not lie in S; in particular, we may assume, without loss of generality, that T has cardinality \geq 2g_X+1, where g_X is the genus of X. Write D \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sum_{t\in T}[t] for the effective divisor on X obtained by taking the formal sum of the points in T, each with multiplicity one; denote the associated line bundle \mathcal{O}_X(D) by \mathcal{L} and the canonical bundle of X by \omega_X. Also, we shall write s_0 \in \Gamma(X,\mathcal{L}) for the section [uniquely determined up to a \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^{\times}-multiple] whose zero divisor is D. Thus, the degree \deg(\mathcal{L}) of \mathcal{L} is \geq 2g_X+1\geq 1. In particular, if x\in X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}), then \deg(\omega_X\otimes\mathcal{L}^{-1}(x))\leq(2g_X-2)-(2g_X+1)+1=-2 so \Gamma(X,\omega_X\otimes\mathcal{L}^{-1}(x))=0. Since, by Serre duality, \Gamma(X,\omega_X\otimes\mathcal{L}^{-1}(x)) is dual to H^1(X,\mathcal{L}(-x)), we thus conclude that H^1(X,\mathcal{L}(-x))=0. Now if we consider the long exact cohomology sequence associated to the exact sequence of coherent sheaves on X 0\to\mathcal{L}(-x)\to\mathcal{L}\to\mathcal{L}\otimes k(x)\to 0 [where k(x) is the residue field of X at x] we obtain an exact sequence \ldots\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})\to\mathcal{L}\otimes k(x)\to H^1(X,\mathcal{L}(-x))\to\ldots — i.e., we have a surjection \Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{L}\otimes k(x). Since \overline{\mathbb{Q}} is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L}) such that s_1(t)\ne0 for all t\in T. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections s_0, s_1 of \mathcal{L} has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism \psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} such that the pull-back by \psi of the unique [up to isomorphism] line bundle of degree 1 on \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} is isomorphic to \mathcal{L}; \psi maps every t\in T to the point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}. Moreover, since every point of the support of D has multiplicity one in D, \psi is unramified over the point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}; since no point of S lies in the support of D, this point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} does not lie in the set \psi(S).
quotations.supports: A real divisor D on the smooth proper curve, its associated line bundle, and canonical bundle omega_X appear in the parent geometric proof.
quotations.does_not_establish: No formula for the divisor of du, local e-1 or -e-1 coefficient, finite support of that coefficient function, or Finsupp construction is stated here.

quotations.exact_quotation: Thus, in summary, by replacing X by \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, T by the point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, and S by the union of \psi(S) and the points of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} over which \psi ramifies, we conclude that we may reduce to the case X=\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, T=\{\beta\}, for some \beta\in\mathbb{P}^1(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\backslash\{\infty\}.
quotations.source_paragraph: Thus, in summary, by replacing X by \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, T by the point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, and S by the union of \psi(S) and the points of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} over which \psi ramifies, we conclude that we may reduce to the case X=\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, T=\{\beta\}, for some \beta\in\mathbb{P}^1(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\backslash\{\infty\}. Next, by applying Lemma 2.4, one reduces to the case X=\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, S\subseteq\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q}), T=\{\beta\}, for some \beta\in\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})\backslash\{\infty\}.
quotations.supports: The parent Belyi proof explicitly uses the branch values of the same finite morphism.
quotations.does_not_establish: The quoted sentence uses branch values in a reduction; it does not separately state or prove the local formal theorem {P | 1 < ramIdx M hDVR u P}.Finite.

quotations.author: Shinichi Mochizuki
quotations.title: Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position
quotations.exact_quotation: Write \omega_X for the canonical sheaf on X. Suppose that U_X is a hyperbolic curve — i.e., that the degree of the line bundle \omega_X(D) is positive.
quotations.source_paragraph:
Theorem 2.1.    (Compactly Bounded Subsets and the ABC Conjecture)
Let Σ be a ﬁnite set of prime numbers.  Then in the terminology of §1 [cf., espe-
cially, Deﬁnitions 1.2, 1.5; Example 1.3; Remarks 1.4.1, 1.5.1], the following two
statements are equivalent:

     (i) (Eﬀective Mordell/ABC/Vojta Conjecture) Let X be a smooth, proper,
geometrically connected curve  over a  number  ﬁeld;  D  ⊆  X  a  reduced  divisor;
UX   def=  X\D;  d a positive integer;  ϵ ∈  R>0 a positive real number.  Write ωX
for the canonical sheaf on X. Suppose that UX is a hyperbolic curve — i.e., that
the degree of the line bundle ωX(D) is positive. Then the inequality of BD-classes
of functions
                        htωX(D)  ≲  (1 + ϵ)(log-diﬀX + log-condD)

holds on UX(Q)≤d.

     (ii) (ABC Conjecture for Σ-Supported Compactly Bounded Subsets)
Let P  def=  P1Q be the projective line over  Q; C ⊆ P  the divisor consisting of the
three points “0”, “1”, and “∞”;  UP            def=  P\C;  d a positive integer;  ϵ ∈  R>0 a
positive real number; KV ⊆ UP(Q) a compactly bounded subset [i.e., regarded
as a subset of P(Q) — cf. Example 1.3, (ii)] whose support contains Σ. Write
ωP for the canonical sheaf on P. Then the inequality of BD-classes of functions

                        htωP(C)  ≲  (1 + ϵ)(log-diﬀP + log-condC)

holds on KV ⋂ UP(Q)≤d.
quotations.supports: Downstream parent context: canonical sheaf in the height inequality. This is an optional secondary citation.
quotations.does_not_establish: It neither constructs the canonical divisor from the actual Fermat coordinate u nor proves its finite support.
